proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Single-model baselines are close together (0.862-0.870), with uni2h+meta best at 0.8701. The tuned members prefer strong regularization: C=1e-4 to 1e-3, and no PCA except where noted.
REASONING: Start exploration with the simplest robust fusion: late_tuned with mean_prob. Each member runs at its own tuned setting, and averaging probabilities is low-variance with no extra fitted parameters. This maps whether simple ensembling of near-equal, partly complementary models gives a gain.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.875-0.885, a modest gain over 0.8701 from reduced variance. If it is at or below 0.870, the models are largely redundant (plausible, since they share attention weights), and fusion gains must come from weighting or stacking rather than averaging.

ANALYSIS: Late_tuned mean_prob reaches 0.8768, about 0.007 above the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.8701), with a lower fold SD. That fits the usual small ensemble gain. Early fusion, gated, early_tuned and the other combiners are all still untested.
REASONING: The exploration phase should map every method. Early fusion is the most standard alternative, so it comes next. With 5632 features and 134 patients, it needs strong regularisation. The tuned members preferred C of 1e-4 to 1e-3, so I use C=0.001 with balance_blocks=true (so Virchow2's larger block does not dominate) and l2_normalize=true, which suited UNI2-h.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.865-0.875, similar to or slightly below late_tuned. If it clearly beats 0.877, then joint linear fusion captures feature interactions across models and early/early_tuned variants deserve more trials. If it is much lower, C is probably mis-set or early fusion is overfitting, and I will lean towards late methods.

ANALYSIS: Both fusions so far (late_tuned mean_prob 0.877, early L2+balanced C=0.001 0.878) beat the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) by ~0.007-0.008. That gain is probably near the acceptance threshold. Per-class gains are small and spread across classes; Papillary and Lepidic stay weakest.
REASONING: We are still exploring, so untested methods should be mapped first. early_tuned keeps each member's tuned preprocessing and learns block weights by inner CV, which could approximate a better per-block C. Virchow2 and H-optimus-1 were tuned at C=1e-4 and uni2h at 1e-3, so a shared C=0.001 with meta_weight=3 is a reasonable midpoint that block weights can shrink further.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.875-0.885. If it is clearly below the early trial (#2), learned block weights are adding inner-CV noise at n=134. In that case I will prefer simple fixed balancing and mapping late/gated.

ANALYSIS: All three fusion families tried so far land around 0.877-0.880 AUROC, about 0.008-0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Early and early_tuned are slightly ahead of late_tuned mean_prob, but the differences are within noise. Papillary (0.78-0.79) and Lepidic (0.82-0.84) are the weakest classes in every trial. Gated, late with a shared config, and the stacking combiners have not been tested.
REASONING: Exploration should cover the untested gated method. It is the one family that could plausibly learn per-patient model weighting. To limit overfitting with only 134 training patients per fold, I use strong regularisation: PCA 32 per model, a small hidden size (32), dropout 0.5, weight_decay 0.1, and a moderate number of epochs (200) at lr 0.001. L2 normalisation follows the uni2h finding, and meta_weight=3 matches the best early trials.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.86-0.88 AUROC with a larger fold SD than the linear methods. If it falls below about 0.87, I will conclude that a learned gate overfits at this sample size and drop the gated method, focusing instead on early/early_tuned C and meta_weight and on late stacking. If it exceeds 0.88, a couple of follow-up gated variants with different regularisation are justified.

ANALYSIS: All three linear fusions (late_tuned mean_prob 0.877, early 0.878, early_tuned 0.880) beat the best single+meta baseline (0.870) by about 0.007-0.010. Gated (0.869) is no better than UNI2-h alone. Papillary (0.78-0.79) and Lepidic (0.82-0.84) are the weakest classes in every method. Plain late fusion with a shared C, and the other combiners, are still untested.
REASONING: In exploration it pays to map the untested methods and knobs. Plain late fusion with a shared setting needs testing. I use l2=True and C=0.001 (UNI2-h's tuned setting, which also worked for early) with mean_logit, a combiner not yet tried. This shows whether the geometric mean beats mean_prob and whether shared settings do better or worse than each member's tuned settings.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.875-0.88, similar to late_tuned mean_prob. If it is clearly lower, the members' own tuned settings matter and late_tuned or early_tuned is the better direction. If it is higher, a shared L2 at C=0.001 is a good common regime, and late with stack or learned_weights is worth testing next.

ANALYSIS: All linear fusions (late, early, early_tuned, late_tuned) land at 0.877-0.881, about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870), with the per-class AUROC profiles nearly identical. Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weak classes. The gated network (0.869) does not beat linear fusion. The knobs not yet mapped are the regularisation strength C (only 0.001 and late_tuned's per-model settings tried), PCA, and the stack/learned_weights combiners.
REASONING: This is still the exploration phase, so I want to map the knob most likely to matter: the strength of regularisation in the early concatenation. With 6,000+ columns and 134 patients, the effective C matters. C=0.0001 with L2 normalisation is very strong shrinkage; combined with balance_blocks it tests whether heavier pooling across models helps the weak classes. Alternatively, PCA could reduce noise. I choose early with PCA=64 and C=0.01. This tests whether dimension reduction plus weaker shrinkage changes the picture, a different region from trial #2.
EXPECTED: If PCA=64 helps, AUROC should be at least about 0.885, with gains in Papillary or Lepidic. If it lands at about 0.87 or lower, PCA discards useful signal, and the linear-fusion plateau is set by the full embeddings at strong shrinkage. In that case the remaining exploration should go to the combiners (stack, learned_weights) and meta_weight rather than to dimension reduction.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusions without PCA cluster at 0.877-0.881, about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Late mean_logit with L2 and C=0.001 is the top result so far. Adding PCA64 with a higher C hurt early fusion (0.862), and gated is weaker (0.869). Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) stay the hardest classes for every method.
REASONING: Still exploring. A key open question is whether learned combination (stack) adds anything over simple averaging. Stacking on the tuned members lets the second-level model reweight members per class, which could help Papillary and Lepidic. I use strong stack regularisation (stack_C=0.01) because inner-CV predictions on about 134 patients are noisy.
EXPECTED: Roughly 0.875-0.885 if stacking is stable. If it falls below the mean_prob result (0.877), learned combiners overfit at this sample size, and later trials should stick to fixed averaging (mean_logit) and tune C and L2 instead.

ANALYSIS: All the simple fusions land at 0.877-0.881 AUROC, about 0.007-0.011 above uni2h+meta (0.870). The best so far is late, mean_logit, L2, C=0.001 (0.8808). Stacking (0.8686), PCA-64 with C=0.01 (0.8622) and gated (0.8694) are worse; the extra flexibility seems to overfit at n=134 per fold. Strong shrinkage (C around 0.001) without PCA is consistently good.
REASONING: Two exploration trials remain. The main open questions are the C level and whether learned_weights helps. Late fusion with mean_logit at C=0.0001 tests stronger shrinkage, which the virchow2 and hoptimus1 baselines preferred. Alternatively, early with C=0.0001 tests the same in a single model. I pick late with mean_logit, L2 and C=0.0001. It changes one knob from the current top config, so the paired comparison is clean and it maps the C axis.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.878-0.884. If it is clearly lower, C=0.001 is the sweet spot and I would next explore C=0.01 or learned_weights. If it is similar, the fusion gain sits on a plateau near 0.88 and is probably limited by the shared signal across models.

ANALYSIS: Fusion consistently reaches ~0.877-0.881, about +0.008-0.011 over the best single model, uni2h+meta (0.870). Late mean_logit with L2, C=0.001 and meta_weight=3 is best so far at 0.8808. Lower C (0.0001) hurt late, and PCA hurt early. Stacking and the gated net underperform, consistent with overfitting at n=134 per fold. Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) remain the weakest classes.
REASONING: One exploration slot remains. Late fusion's C has been tested only at 0.0001 and 0.001, and the lower value was worse, so C=0.01 checks whether the optimum lies on the less-regularised side. This settles the main open knob for the leading method before acceptance testing begins.
EXPECTED: If AUROC lands at ~0.88 or above, the late-fusion optimum spans C 0.001-0.01, and C=0.01 or meta_weight can be refined. If it drops (<0.875), C=0.001 is the optimum, and the remaining budget should go to combine rules (learned_weights) and meta_weight rather than C.

ANALYSIS: All fusion methods with heavy regularisation (C≈0.001, no PCA, L2-normalised) land around 0.877–0.881, only about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870). Late mean_logit at C=0.001 is the top so far (0.8808); it is peaked in C, since 0.0001 and 0.01 are both worse. PCA=64 hurt early fusion, and stacking or gating underperform, probably from overfitting with 134 patients per fold. Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.82) are the weak classes.
REASONING: This is the last exploration slot, so it should answer an open question rather than chase noise. The meta_weight knob is untested: every trial used 3. The uni2h tuned baseline preferred meta_weight=10, and metadata alone reaches 0.60 AUROC. Testing late mean_logit at C=0.001 with meta_weight=10 isolates this knob around the current best. It shows whether less shrinkage of age/sex adds signal on top of the image models.
EXPECTED: I expect a small change, roughly ±0.005. If AUROC goes above about 0.883, metadata weighting matters and I will explore meta_weight=10 in early_tuned and early fusion. If it drops or stays flat, I will fix meta_weight=3 and focus on the combination rule (e.g. learned_weights) or early_tuned C, accepting that gains over 0.88 may be hard to make significant.
decision_reason: exploration phase: nothing is accepted; end of exploration: trial 5 (highest mean AUROC of the 10 explored trials) becomes the current best

proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: All fusion methods land between 0.869 and 0.881, about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Late mean_logit with L2, no PCA, C=0.001 and meta_weight=3 is the current best at 0.8808. Its C is already bracketed: 1e-4 gave 0.872 and 1e-2 gave 0.875. PCA=64 hurt early fusion, and stacking and the gated network were weaker. Differences of about 0.005 are within noise.
REASONING: The cheapest open question for the current best is L2 normalisation. Virchow2 and H-optimus-1 each preferred no L2 on their own, so turning L2 off inside late mean_logit at the same C could change how the members are calibrated. learned_weights is another untested combiner, but with equal-quality members it is unlikely to beat a simple mean by a clear margin. The meta_weight question is partly answered: 10 gave 0.8755, so 1 is a lower-priority check. Testing l2_normalize=False answers a real question about the space.
EXPECTED: Likely within ±0.005 of 0.8808, so not accepted. A clear drop would confirm that L2 helps the shared-C setup. A gain larger than the threshold (about 0.01) is unlikely. If it fails, the remaining checks are learned_weights and meta_weight=1, and then I would accept that #5 is near the ceiling.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives a consistent but small gain (~+0.01 over uni2h+meta 0.870). The best is late mean_logit with L2, C=0.001, meta 3 (0.8808). Early_tuned (0.8796) and early with balanced blocks (0.8784) are close behind. C=0.001 is clearly the sweet spot, while PCA and stacking hurt. The acceptance threshold is very small (~0.0015), so paired differences are tight.
REASONING: Untested combiners on the best late config remain: learned_weights could upweight uni2h, and mean_prob behaves differently from mean_logit. Of these, mean_prob is the closest variant. learned_weights answers a more informative question: is equal weighting suboptimal? Uni2h is the strongest member, so learned weights might give a small paired gain. That would answer an open question at low cost.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.878-0.884. If it fails to beat #5, equal geometric averaging is already near-optimal. Learned weights at n=134 would then just add noise, and I would move on to probing early_tuned C/meta or the early balance_blocks variants.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusion gives a modest gain (~0.88 vs 0.870 for uni2h+meta). Late mean_logit with L2, C=0.001, meta_weight=3 is the best; neighbouring settings of C, meta_weight and L2 are all lower or within noise. Early and early_tuned are close (0.878-0.880). PCA hurt in early fusion, gated underperformed, and stack and learned_weights did not help.
REASONING: Two open questions remain. One is whether PCA helps in late fusion, where each member is a separate low-sample LR. The other is whether early fusion without balance_blocks, or with a different meta_weight, behaves differently. PCA=64 hurt early fusion, but that was at C=0.01. Combined with mean_logit, a smaller PCA (32) plus a higher C might regularise differently and diversify the members. Still, the evidence favours no PCA. A more plausible gain is early_tuned with meta_weight=10, since metadata helped uni2h most at weight 10. That change is small, though. I'll test late with pca=128 at C=0.01: a distinct regularisation regime (dimension reduction versus heavy shrinkage) that tells us whether PCA is dead for fusion.
EXPECTED: Likely 0.870-0.880, no acceptance. If it is clearly below the best, I drop PCA entirely and focus on early_tuned meta/C variations and late weighted_vote. If it beats 0.881 by more than the threshold, I explore PCA 64/128 with C values nearby.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusion beats the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) by about 0.01 AUROC. The current best is late fusion with shared C=0.001, L2 normalisation, meta_weight=3 and mean_logit (#5, 0.8808). Nearby changes to C, meta_weight, L2, PCA and learned_weights were all slightly worse, so that neighbourhood looks flat. The one stacking trial (late_tuned, stack_C=0.01) was clearly worse (0.8686, BA 0.469), probably because the meta-learner was over-regularised.
REASONING: Stacking is the only combiner that can learn class-specific trust in each model, and the per-class AUROCs differ somewhat between members (e.g. Micropapillary and Papillary). The only stacking evidence comes from a strongly shrunk meta-learner on tuned members. Testing stack with stack_C=0.1 on the best base setting answers whether a less-regularised stacker can add signal beyond equal-weight geometric averaging. Simple tweaks of the already-mapped late/early knobs are unlikely to clear the threshold.
EXPECTED: If class-specific weighting helps, AUROC should reach about 0.885 or more, with gains in the classes where the models disagree. If it comes in at or below 0.88, the base probabilities are too noisy at this sample size to learn weights. I would then conclude that equal-weight averaging is near-optimal and turn to early_tuned C/meta variations or stop.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives a consistent but small lift over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Late mean_logit with shared L2, C=0.001 and meta_weight=3 leads at 0.881. Many variants cluster at 0.875-0.880: L2 off, learned weights, stacking, PCA, and early or early_tuned fusion. In this regime C=0.001 is the sweet spot, and C=0.0001 and C=0.01 both lose about 0.006. Late_tuned members and gating underperform.
REASONING: Early_tuned was run only at C=0.001. Its block weights are capped at 1, so the effective per-block strength C×w² can only shrink from the base C. At C=0.001 the inner CV can only regularise blocks more strongly, never less. Raising the base C to 0.01 lets the inner CV pick effective strengths of about 0.01, 0.0025 or 0.000625 per block. That makes early_tuned a genuinely more flexible per-model regulariser and tests whether per-block shrinkage beats late averaging.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.880-0.886. That only counts if the gain over #5 clears the threshold (about 0.005), which is uncertain. If it lands at or below 0.88, per-block tuning of early fusion adds nothing over late mean_logit. I would then treat about 0.88 as the fusion ceiling and spend the remaining trials on only a few distinct checks, such as late_tuned mean_logit and a more regularised gated model, rather than fine-tuning.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives a consistent but small gain over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870): late mean_logit with L2, C=0.001, meta 3 (#5, 0.881) is best, and early/early_tuned/stack variants land within noise (0.878-0.880). Stronger C (0.01) consistently hurts (#6, #9, #15), and PCA does not help. Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) remain the weakest classes.
REASONING: Within early_tuned, C=0.01 lost clearly to C=0.001, which suggests stronger shrinkage may help further. Two of the three members (Virchow2, H-optimus-1) were individually tuned to C=0.0001, and the learned block weights can only weaken blocks further. C=0.0001 is the untested end of this trend, and it is the most plausible remaining route to a non-trivial gain in a different fusion family. It also answers whether early_tuned is regularisation-limited.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.878-0.885. A gain above the threshold (~0.005) would establish early_tuned with strong shrinkage as the best fusion. If it is flat or worse, the C optimum for joint fusion is about 0.001, and both fusion families are saturated near 0.88. I would then probe only a few remaining distinct options (gated with stronger regularisation, late meta_weight=1) before accepting #5.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion with a shared setting (L2, no PCA, meta_weight 3, C=0.001, mean_logit) is best at 0.8808. That beats uni2h+meta (0.870) by about 0.011. Neighbours in C, meta_weight, L2, combine rule and PCA all land at 0.872-0.880 and are rejected, so the late family looks like a flat plateau. Early, early_tuned and gated are no better. Stacking raises balanced accuracy (0.543) but not AUROC.
REASONING: One clean, untested question remains: per-model tuned members (late_tuned) combined with mean_logit, the rule that won in the shared-config late family. Trial #1 tested late_tuned only with mean_prob (0.8768). Virchow2 and H-optimus run at C=1e-4 without L2 in their tuned configs, which may change the logit scale and diversity under a geometric mean. This is a cheap, direct test of whether member-level tuning adds anything beyond a shared C.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.877-0.882, likely not accepted. If it is clearly below #5, then a shared, moderately regularised C=0.001 is better for fusion than per-model tuning. In that case I would try the remaining structurally different options (low-dimensional PCA in late fusion, or a more strongly regularised gated model) before accepting that the plateau is about 0.88.

ANALYSIS: Fusion is consistently about 0.875–0.881 against 0.870 for the best single model (uni2h+meta). Trial #5 (late, L2, C=0.001, meta_weight=3, mean_logit) leads at 0.8808. Its close neighbours (C, meta_weight, L2, PCA, combine rule) all scored within noise or worse. Moving C away from 0.001 or adding PCA hurts, and stacking and learned weights add variance without gain.
REASONING: The late family around #5 looks saturated. One structural question in early fusion is still open: balance_blocks was always True. Without balancing, Virchow2's 2560 columns carry more total variance. This is effectively a different block weighting, and the inner-CV block weights in early_tuned hinted that weighting matters. The trial keeps the otherwise best early setting (#2) so the comparison is clean.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC of about 0.875–0.880, i.e. no clear gain, which would confirm that block balancing is neutral or helpful and that early fusion is capped near 0.88. A gain above the threshold, around 0.885 or more, would point to Virchow2 deserving more weight, and I would then explore unbalanced early fusion with nearby C values.

ANALYSIS: All linear fusions cluster at 0.875-0.881 AUROC, about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). C=0.001 with L2 and meta_weight=3 is a clear optimum for late fusion. Combine rule, block balancing, L2 and early vs late all change results by less than the noise threshold. Gated fusion (0.869) underperforms, and PCA hurts. Seven trials remain before the stop rule triggers.
REASONING: The large unexplored region is the gated network. Only one config has been tried, and it used PCA=32, which hurt the linear models too. A gated run without PCA, with a small hidden size and strong regularisation, is the remaining plausible route to a clear gain, because a per-patient gate could help on classes like Papillary and Acinar. Further linear variants of the knobs already tried are unlikely to clear the threshold.
EXPECTED: If the gated model with full-dimensional L2-normalised inputs, hidden=16, dropout 0.5 and wd 0.1 reaches at least 0.885, it could be accepted. If it stays at or below 0.875, I will conclude that the adaptive gate adds nothing beyond linear late fusion and that the fusion ceiling is about 0.88.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.876-0.881 AUROC. The accepted best is #5 (late, L2, C=0.001, meta_weight=3, mean_logit) at 0.8808, about +0.011 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.8701). Changing C, PCA, L2, the combiner, block balancing or the tuned variants all gave paired gains at or below zero. Gated networks are clearly worse, and PCA consistently hurts.
REASONING: One plausible lever around the best is still unmapped: lower metadata weight. meta_weight=10 lowered AUROC (0.8755 vs 0.8808), and metadata alone is weak (0.60), so less weight on age/sex might help the image signal. meta_weight=1.0 has not been tried for late fusion. It is a cheap check of whether the meta trend continues downward. The other open directions (gated variants, PCA) have negative evidence.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC of about 0.878-0.882, i.e. within noise of #5 and rejected. If it is clearly better (above about 0.885) it would be accepted, and metadata over-weighting was a hidden cost. If it fails, that confirms meta_weight=3 is near optimal and late mean_logit at C=0.001 is the fusion ceiling. Remaining trials would then serve only to confirm the plateau before the stop rule triggers.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusions cluster tightly around 0.877-0.881 AUROC. Late mean_logit at L2, C=0.001 and meta_weight 1-3 (#5, #20) is the best, about +0.011 over uni2h+meta. Shared-C sweeps, PCA, balance_blocks, stacking and learned weights all fail to beat it, and the gated network underperforms, especially without PCA. The landscape looks flat near its optimum, and only 5 non-improving trials remain before the stop.
REASONING: The main untested knobs are smaller PCA in late fusion (32), which no linear method has tried, and the weighted_vote combiner. A PCA of 32 per model with a larger C (0.1) is a different regularisation regime: low-rank features with weak shrinkage. It could help the weak classes (Papillary, Lepidic) if the high-dimensional ridge is underfitting. PCA 64 hurt in early fusion and PCA 128 was neutral in late fusion, so this is a real open question rather than chasing noise.
EXPECTED: Most likely a similar or slightly lower AUROC (about 0.87). If it does not beat #5 by the threshold, I conclude that dimensionality reduction does not help. In that case the full-dimensional, strongly ridge-regularised late mean_logit fusion is the practical optimum, and #5 stands as the fusion result.

ANALYSIS: Every reasonable linear fusion falls in the 0.876-0.881 range, which is about +0.01 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Shared-C late/mean_logit at C=0.001 with L2 normalisation (#5) is the best. Neighbouring settings of C, meta_weight, L2, PCA and the combine rule all come out at or below #5, inside the noise. Gated networks are clearly worse. The surface is flat, and only 4 trials remain before the stop rule.
REASONING: One combination is still untested: late with mean_prob, the arithmetic mean of probabilities. It is a different averaging rule from geometric mean_logit and could plausibly behave differently on the weak classes, Papillary and Lepidic. The other choice that changes calibration, stack, already gave the best BA (0.543) but no AUROC gain. A large gain is unlikely anywhere, so a cheap, distinct combine choice at the best member settings is a reasonable probe that also answers an open question.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.878-0.881, which would be rejected. If so, I conclude that the choice of combine rule doesn't matter at this setting. The fusion gain over single models (about +0.01) is real, but #5 is effectively at the plateau, so the search should end with #5 as the fusion config.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.876-0.881 AUROC. The best is late mean_logit with L2 and C=0.001 (0.8808), about +0.011 over uni2h+meta. Changing combine rule, meta_weight, or L2 within late moves AUROC by less than 0.002. PCA, higher C and the gated network all hurt clearly. Early fusion has only been tried with L2 on and C≥0.001, which does not match the setting Virchow2 and H-optimus-1 preferred alone (no L2, C=0.0001).
REASONING: Three trials remain before the stop rule. The one untested region with a plausible mechanism for a clear gain is early fusion with raw standardised features and strong shrinkage (C=0.0001), with balanced blocks so Virchow2's 2560 columns do not dominate. This matches the regime two of the three members preferred alone. A joint model in that regime could exploit complementary directions across models that late averaging cannot.
EXPECTED: Expected AUROC is about 0.878-0.885. Acceptance needs a gain above the threshold of roughly 0.003-0.005. If it falls short, early fusion is no better than late averaging in any regularisation regime. I would then conclude that 0.88 is the fusion ceiling, about +0.01 over the best single model, and that #5 should be kept.

ANALYSIS: Fusion consistently reaches about 0.878-0.881 AUROC, versus 0.870 for the best single model (uni2h+meta). The best is late mean_logit at C=0.001 with L2 normalisation (#5). Its neighbours (meta_weight, C, combiner, L2, PCA, early vs early_tuned) all land within ±0.003 of it. PCA, larger C and gated networks are clearly worse. This is a plateau. Among the combiners, stack (#14, stack_C=0.1) gave the highest balanced accuracy (0.543) and the best Lepidic AUROC (0.86). Its AUROC tied #5, but its paired-gain variance was high (threshold 0.011).
REASONING: Only two trials remain before the stop rule fires, so the remaining open question should be the one with some upside. Stacking is the only combiner that changes how classes are weighted per model, and it showed a distinct per-class profile. Its weakness was variance from fitting the second-level model on inner-CV predictions of only about 134 patients. A stronger stack penalty (stack_C=0.01) on the strong #5 base members should cut that variance while keeping the per-class reweighting. The late_tuned stack at 0.01 did poorly (0.869), but its base members were the weaker tuned ones (C=0.0001 for two models), not the #5 setting.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.880-0.885 with lower fold variance and balanced accuracy around 0.52-0.54. If the gain does not clear the threshold, the stack adds nothing beyond simple averaging. I would then conclude that late mean_logit (#5) is the final fusion, about +0.011 over uni2h+meta, and that the remaining differences are noise.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusions all land near 0.877-0.884, with fold SDs around 0.03. Late fusion with C=0.001, L2 and meta_weight 3 is the accepted best (#5, 0.8808). PCA, larger C and gated networks hurt clearly. The one positive signal is stacking on these base models: stack_C=0.01 gave +0.0034 (BA 0.527, better Lepidic and In situ), while stack_C=0.1 was worse. That points to stronger shrinkage of the stacker helping.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule fires, so it should go to the direction with a measured positive trend. Lowering stack_C from 0.1 to 0.01 raised AUROC by about 0.005. Going to 0.001 continues that trend, regularising the 21+2-feature stacker harder on only about 134 patients. That should cut the fold variance that set the 0.009 threshold, while keeping the stacker's data-driven reweighting of age/sex and per-class base logits.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.884-0.888 with lower per-fold variance, possibly clearing the threshold. If it falls back toward 0.880 or below, the stacking gain is noise and the stacker either underfits or merely approximates mean_logit. The conclusion would then be that fusion gives a modest but real gain over uni2h+meta (about +0.01), and #5 stays the final choice.
